title: Thai SEC says attackers used stolen usernames and passwords to reach personal data of 155 users
date_note: Fintech News Singapore (27 Nov) says the regulator detected the breach on 25 November.
geo_basis: Thai SEC, a national agency; Bangkok coordinates
summary: Fintech News Singapore reports that a data breach at Thailand's SEC exposed personal information belonging to 155 users across 10 organisations. SEC spokesperson Anek Yoo-yin said attackers had obtained usernames and passwords of authorised users and used those accounts to access the SEC's online systems. The SEC blocked access to its Electronic Information Submission Management System and reported the incident to Thailand's National Cyber Security Agency.
plain: Thailand's SEC says attackers used stolen log-in details of authorised users to get into its online systems. Personal information of 155 users across 10 organisations was exposed, according to the report.
exec: A national securities regulator says stolen user credentials gave attackers access to personal data of 155 users across 10 organisations.
action: The SEC asked affected users to verify their identities and change their passwords to regain access, as reported by Fintech News Singapore.

evidence.quote: exposed personal information belonging to 155 users across 10 organisations

validation.note: Only Fintech News Singapore was read; it relays the SEC's spokesperson. The SEC's own notice was not found.
